method: Round two of 1807, under the rule 'every story alike' (11 November 2026): the items that round one held back for framing, counted item by item at the year's rule of 7 newspapers with phrase searches on all 4,167 pages in both transcriptions, reading of every hit, loose keyword searches of the papers in print without a hit, and scan checks of each admitted passage

new_groups.label: General Wilkinson's speech in the court at New Orleans
new_groups.definition: Printings of General Wilkinson's address to the court at New Orleans, as a letter from that city of 18 December 1806 reports it (Washington, 21 January 1807): appearing on a writ of habeas corpus for a man he had arrested, he said he was 'called to account for an act in which I glory', warned that 'the artifices of the confederates' must no longer 'cheat the public judgment' and that 'treason stalks abroad', and spoke of 'the friends of Burr and rebellion'. The report adds that he then charged two lawyers with being parties to the conspiracy. The general's own words, as the letter gives them.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

new_groups.label: News from Hayti by way of St. Thomas, February 1807
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Baltimore paragraph of 3 February 1807: from papers brought by a gentleman from St. Thomas, an account of 'operations' in 'the republic of Hayti' down to 27 December 1806, 'on which day the new Republican Constitution was adopted'. It says that General Christophe came before Port-au-Prince on 5 December with about 10,000 men 'to compel' the assembly to make him emperor, fired on General 'Pichon', the commander there, who had come out to meet him, and was driven from the town; and that news received at Jacmel on 15 January had him defeated and in flight. Six papers add, after the first sentences, the editor's promise to give the constitution 'without further loss of time than is necessary for a correct translation'. A report at second hand, from papers and news from the republic's side.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

new_groups.label: Robert MacDonald's funeral at Norfolk, June 1807
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Norfolk paragraph of 29 June 1807: Robert MacDonald, 'one of the seamen wounded on board the Chesapeake frigate', died at the Marine Hospital, and his funeral the day before was 'attended by nearly four thousand citizens', with a procession of boats, minute guns, colours at half mast and a sermon at Christ Church; the paper prints the order of the procession. A local report of a public funeral.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

new_groups.label: The National Intelligencer on the seamen the Leopard sought
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Washington paragraph of 29 July 1807 from the National Intelligencer: 'Much error having appeared in the accounts circulated' of what passed between the government and the British minister, Erskine, 'in the case of the seamen, to obtain whom the Leopard made the late attack on the Chesapeake', it states that his application for their surrender was refused, that naval commanders had orders not to recruit British deserters, and that the government had reason to believe the seamen were native citizens of the United States. The National Intelligencer's own account; it adds a note with the seamen's names and particulars as Captain Barron reported them.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1807 printings, checked against the scan (round two: stories once held back for framing, at the year's 7-paper rule).

dispositions_summary.method: Round two of 1807. On 11 November 2026 the owner set the rule 'every story alike': a reviewed story is described by what kind of text it is and whose account, in the papers' own words, never as what happened; sensitive subjects get no special treatment. Items that earlier rounds held back for framing are therefore counted by the year's own rule, exactly like any other item: what reaches it is admitted, what does not stays out. As before, an excerpt ends before the names of private people where it can, and stories that turn on private people stay out. The five items round one listed for the owner to decide were read again with phrase searches over all 4,167 pages of 1807 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), every hit was read, the papers in print without a hit were searched with loose keywords, and every admitted printing was checked against its page scan by AI reviewers (scan_batches/batch_12.json and batch_13.json, SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points_round2.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As in round one: a story needs one printed item found in 7 or more newspapers, counted item by item. Round one admitted every item in 9 or more papers and chose among the items in 7 or 8 to cover the months and kinds of news; this round admits every once-held-back item that reaches 7, as the round was set. The new stories are top-level: the parent stories of round one (Burr's conspiracy, the Chesapeake affair) name their children in their definitions and stay as released.

counted_item_by_item.The Hayti report: 9 papers (NI and ADA 4 February, EN 6 February, NG 9 February, VA 10 February, HUS 14 February, PGz 16 February, NHG 17 February, BJ 20 February). After its first sentences, six papers print the editor's promise to give the constitution 'without further loss of time' and three (NI, HUS, BJ) go on with the account of 5 December. The EN's printing survives only in the older CA transcription. The ADA also printed the constitution (7 and 10 February), a different item.
counted_item_by_item.Wilkinson's address: 8 papers (NI 21 January, ADA 22 January, VA and EN 27 January, NG 28 January, HUS 31 January, PGz 2 February, NHG 10 February). A fuller report of the same address in other words, printed by NI (4 March) and VA (13 March), is a different item and not counted.
counted_item_by_item.MacDonald's funeral: 7 papers (NG 29 June, ADA and EN 3 July, NI 8 July, BJ 10 July, PGz 13 July, NHG 14 July). Fourth of July toasts that name him with three other seamen (EN 7 July, VA 8 July) are other items.
counted_item_by_item.The seamen paragraph: 8 papers (NI 29 July, ADA 31 July, NG 3 August, EN 4 August, VA 5 August, HUS 8 August, PGz 10 August, NHG 11 August). The NI's commentary of 17 August quotes it and is not counted.

not_admitted.The act to prohibit the importation of s: Printed in full 'by authority' in 5 papers: NI 6 March, a VA extra of 14 April, HUS 2 May, NHG 20 October (where RevX shortens it with '...') and an EN extra of 13 November. Below the rule, like the other laws printed by authority in fewer than 7 papers.
